correctness.rationale: The divisor identity factors C_n as M D Z^T with integral unimodular Möbius and zeta incidence factors. Thus the Gram is integrally equivalent to D(Z^T Z)D, not to the square of the Smith normal form of C_n. For p^a, U=Z^T Z has entries a+1−max(i,j), and differencing neighboring rows and columns of a leading i×i block gives determinant L=a−i+2. When the eliminated prefix U-block is a local unit, each of its remaining cross-columns is (a−j+1) times the all-ones vector, and its inverse sends that vector to its last basis vector divided by L. This gives the claimed residual formula. In the one-index branch the residual diagonal is a unit times p^(2i). In the pair branch the unweighted residual two-block has unit determinant as a−i is a unit; its weighted block has entries divisible by p^(2i+1) and, after division by that power, unit determinant. Elimination of either block is integral: with pivot indices I and later indices J, the multiplier is D_J R_JI R_II^(-1) D_I^(-1), whose entry for j∈J and ℓ∈I includes p^(j−ℓ) and a local-integer factor. The enlarged unweighted prefix is again a unit in both branches, proving the scan inductively (including an empty prefix and the final index). Coprime tensor factors are invertible at p except for the p-factor itself, so local Smith powers repeat with the stated multiplicity and global factors align in sorted order. The product gives n^τ(n); for odd p the last exponent is 2a, and for p=2 the last two indices necessarily form a pair so the last exponent is 2a−1. Only index zero could give a unit, which yields the stated rank. The empty product at n=1 yields (1). As finite corroboration, 75 independently constructed integer Smith computations using a totient-quotient formula for the entries agreed, including prime-power exponents up to 12 and mixed moduli.

evidence: Theorem 1.1 of the gcd-matrix paper diagonalizes (f(gcd(x_i,x_j))) on factor-closed sets by unimodular Möbius congruence. For the prime chain and f=τ it gives diag(1,...,1) for U. Theorem 1.2 addresses power-LCM matrices, not this scaling. The Ramanujan supercharacter result diagonalizes a column-weighted product, and supplies the coprime tensor factorization.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Congruence of U to I cannot be pushed through D using unimodular operations in general, because D has nonunit diagonal at p. The column weights in the supercharacter orthogonality are not generally units either. A normal form for either easier matrix is not a broader classification of the unweighted Gram.

evidence: Schlage-Puchta's theorem exactly implies |det G_n|=n^τ(n) by squaring. The unscaled U normal form gives a unit determinant, not the individual valuations of DUD. At p=2,a=1 the weighted core is [[2,2],[2,4]], with Smith factors 2,2; replacing U by I would give 1,4.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The determinant is genuinely covered and is not counted as distinct. The two-index example shows why the published U normal form alone does not imply simply squaring the weights. Determining which neighboring valuations pair for all a requires the local analysis.

evidence: The supercharacter table S(n)_{i,j}=c_{d_i}(n/d_j) is C_n with permuted columns, which does preserve the unweighted row Gram. Transposing the table in the determinant paper preserves its determinant, not automatically the Smith form of the corresponding row Gram. After reversing prime-power indices, U is a gcd matrix with f=τ on a divisor chain.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The known table and the chain description are true overlaps, but no inspected statement applies a Gram Smith classification to that table. originality.rationale: The published table, its coprime factorization, its weighted orthogonality and the Gram determinant are prior mathematics. A general gcd-matrix normal form also covers the unscaled core U. The supported distinct claim is the full integral Smith classification of the unweighted Gram, especially the local pairs at indices i with p dividing a−i+1. None of the compared statements supplies the Smith classification after the nonunimodular weights D on both sides.
residual_risks: The power-GCD/LCM divisibility article could not be inspected; a relevant theorem there or in an unindexed treatment of weighted chain matrices is not ruled out. The decision credits only the distinct Gram classification, not priority certification or novelty of the determinant.

value.rationale: The unweighted Gram on the natural divisor-indexed Ramanujan table has an integral cokernel that neither its determinant nor the standard weighted orthogonality identifies. The paired exponents explain departures from naive squared Smith factors and give the full finite abelian group, its exponent, and the modular rank behavior for all n. These are reusable precise invariants for that standard table, not an arbitrary slice or recomputation of its determinant.
residual_risks: This assessment concerns exactly the all-divisor unweighted row Gram, not weighted or residue-indexed Gram forms.
